title: Archimedean regulators, primitive periods and arithmetic volumes
summary: Construct the actual higher number-field regulator and its integral lattice, prove the primitive-period and zeta covolume theorems including rank zero, and compare the universal Beilinson realization with full gauge and Tate normalizations.

layers.title: Tate coordinates, trace and leading coefficients

targets.name: tateEmbeddingSpace
targets.statement: Define Vₙ(F) as the real subspace of Σ_F → ℂ consisting of functions taking values in (2πi)^(n−1)ℝ and satisfying v(conj σ)=conj(v(σ)). Define Cₙ(F) by requiring these values to lie in (2πi)^(n−1)ℤ. Selection of all real embeddings when n is odd and one embedding per nonreal conjugate pair identifies Vₙ(F) with ℝ^dₙ and Cₙ(F) with ℤ^dₙ, where dₙ=r₁+r₂ for odd n and r₂ for even n. Give Vₙ the transported finite-dimensional norm and coordinate Haar measure of covolume one on Cₙ.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 1

locator.where: Proposition 9.22 and Corollary 9.23, p.85, lines 3650–3709

api.name: tateEmbeddingSpace.ext
api.statement: Two vectors are equal if their values at every embedding agree; selected surviving coordinates already suffice.

api.name: tateEmbeddingCoordinates
api.statement: Coordinate evaluation divided by (2πi)^(n−1) is a real linear equivalence carrying Cₙ onto the standard integer lattice.

api.name: tateEmbeddingSpace.finrank
api.statement: The real dimension is dₙ; the inherited lattice is discrete and spans.

api.name: tateEmbeddingCoordinates_change
api.statement: Permuting selected embeddings gives a permutation matrix. Replacing a complex representative by its conjugate multiplies that coordinate by (-1)^(n−1); these changes preserve coordinate Haar measure.

api.name: tateEmbeddingSpace_topology
api.statement: The coordinate linear equivalence is continuous in both directions for the native subspace topology from Σ_F→ℂ; the transported norm has this same topology. The normalized covolume does not use the ambient product-volume normalization.

tests.name: real_parity
tests.statement: For F=ℚ, n=2 the equation t=-t gives t=0 and dimension 0; n=3 allows every t and has dimension 1. Reversed parity fails both.

tests.name: complex_pair
tests.statement: For ℚ(i), n=2 the divided pair is (t,-t), and n=3 it is (t,t); both spaces have dimension 1, not 2.

tests.name: tate_unit
tests.statement: The selected value (2πi)^(n−1) has coordinate 1; in weight 3 the value is -4π² and still has coordinate 1. An untwisted coordinate would give -4π².

tests.name: zero_space
tests.statement: For a totally real field in even weight, Cₙ=Vₙ={0}; the standard fundamental domain is a point of mass 1.

tests.name: ambient_norm_control
tests.statement: At weight 2 an imaginary pair with divided coordinate 1 has native product sup norm 2π and normalized coordinate norm 1; at weight 3 a real Tate generator has native norm 4π² and normalized norm 1. The topology agrees, but an isometry assertion without these factors is false.

targets.name: embeddingRestrictionTrace
targets.statement: For a finite extension E/F, define R:Vₙ(F)→Vₙ(E) by (Rv)_τ=v_(τ|F), and T:Vₙ(E)→Vₙ(F) by (Tw)_σ=Σ_(τ|σ)w_τ, summing over all embeddings extending σ. Both preserve the coordinate lattices, commute with conjugation, and satisfy T∘R=[E:F]·id. Restriction and trace compose in towers.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 1
E/F is finite, with its specified algebra structure and scalar tower

locator.where: Definition 10.8, p.94, lines 4091–4106, embedding assembly only; the restriction, trace and tower laws are elementary finite-fibre identities

api.name: embeddingRestrictionTrace_apply
api.statement: The displayed coordinate formulas determine the two real linear maps uniquely.

api.name: embeddingTrace_restriction
api.statement: T(R(v))=[E:F]v for every v.

api.name: embeddingTrace_tower
api.statement: For L/E/F, T_L/F=T_E/F∘T_L/E and R_L/F=R_L/E∘R_E/F; identity extensions give identity maps.

tests.name: imaginary_to_real_even
tests.statement: For ℚ(i)/ℚ in weight 2, T(t,-t)=0 in the zero target; averaging only the selected coordinate would give t.

tests.name: imaginary_to_real_odd
tests.statement: For ℚ(i)/ℚ in weight 3, R(t)=(t,t) and T(R(t))=2t. A trace divided by two fails this law.

tests.name: real_quadratic_trace
tests.statement: For a real quadratic extension in odd weight T(a,b)=a+b and R(t)=(t,t); the identity extension gives T(t)=t.

targets.name: dedekindZetaLeadingCoefficient
targets.statement: Using LFunctions Layer 3’s continued Dedekind function, define ζ_F*(1−n) to be the coefficient of (s−(1−n))^dₙ in its analytic germ at 1−n. Prove that the germ has order exactly dₙ, this coefficient is real and nonzero, and it is the punctured limit ζ_F(s)/(s−(1−n))^dₙ. Prove ζ_F*(1−n)∈ℚˣ·√Δ_F·π^(dₙ−Nn)·ζ_F(n), with ζ_F(n)>0 and equal to the pinned convergent value.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2

api.name: dedekindZetaLeadingCoefficient_limit
api.statement: The punctured complex limit is the real leading coefficient embedded in ℂ; at dₙ=0 it is the analytic value.

api.name: dedekindZetaLeadingCoefficient_ne_zero
api.statement: For every n≥2 the coefficient is nonzero and the order is dₙ.

api.name: dedekindZetaLeadingCoefficient_functionalEquation
api.statement: Its ratio to √Δ_F π^(dₙ−Nn) ζ_F(n) is a nonzero rational number.

tests.name: q_weight_two
tests.statement: At F=ℚ,n=2, d=0 and ζ*(-1)=-1/12, whereas ζ(2)/π²=1/6; their ratio is -1/2.

tests.name: q_weight_three
tests.statement: At F=ℚ,n=3, d=1 and ζ*(-2)=ζ′(-2)=-ζ(3)/(4π²); the analytic value ζ(-2)=0 is the wrong leading coefficient.

tests.name: q_weight_four
tests.statement: At F=ℚ,n=4, d=0 and ζ*(-3)=1/120; dividing by ζ(4)/π⁴=1/90 gives 3/4.

tests.name: excluded_weight_one
tests.statement: At n=1, ζ_F has order r₁+r₂−1 at 0, not the odd-weight formula r₁+r₂. For ℚ the two numbers are 0 and 1.

layers.title: Primitive classes and the specified arithmetic regulator

targets.name: normalizedBorelClass
targets.statement: For n≥2 and matrix size b≥2n+1, construct the class Boₙ,b in H_cont^(2n−1)(GL_b(ℂ),ℝ(n−1)). It is the image of the suspended twisted Chern character chₙ under restriction to U(b), invariant-form identification with the compact dual, identity inside the complexified relative cochains, and inverse van Est. Its restrictions along trailing-identity block inclusions agree. Use the ordered complex suspension and the compact generator εₙ obtained from (-1)^n times the clutching class of u^n, where u=O(-1)−1 is TopologicalKTheory’s chosen Bott class. Prove that suspended chₙ evaluates on εₙ to (2πi)^n.
hypotheses: The clutching map is the actual supplier map with ordered complex suspension; εₙ is related to its u=O(-1)−1 by the stated (-1)^n factor

locator.where: Definition 9.24, p.86, lines 3733–3753; Proposition 9.22, p.85, lines 3670–3688

api.name: normalizedBorelClass_stabilize
api.statement: Restriction from b+1 to b preserves Boₙ,b.

api.name: normalizedBorelClass_conjugation
api.statement: Complex conjugation on matrices and ℝ(n−1) together fixes the class.

api.name: normalizedBorelClass_bott
api.statement: Suspended chₙ evaluates on the specified compact homotopy generator εₙ=(-1)^n clutch(u^n) to (2πi)^n; replacing chₙ by the zero class or twice chₙ fails this equation.

tests.name: bott_two
tests.statement: In weight 2 the suspended character evaluates to (2πi)²=-4π²; after dividing by that Tate generator the value is 1.

tests.name: bott_three
tests.statement: In weight 3 the value is (2πi)³=-8π³i and its Tate coordinate is 1; replacing ch₃ by c₃ changes the generator by the factorial 2.

tests.name: stabilized_diagonal
tests.statement: Adding an identity block preserves the reduced universal bundle class and hence adds 0 to the positive-degree character, rather than multiplying its value by the matrix size.

targets.name: numberFieldBorelRegulator
targets.statement: Construct r_Bo:K_(2n−1)(O_F)→Vₙ(F) by mapping to each K_(2n−1)(ℂ), applying the plus/Q comparison and ordinary Hurewicz, and evaluating Boₙ. Use the inverse of the actual rational inclusion K_(2n−1)(O_F)⊗ℚ→K_(2n−1)(F)⊗ℚ to define r_Bo,ℚ on field K-theory. This rational map agrees with the direct embedding construction.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2

locator.where: Definition 9.19 and Proposition 9.21–Corollary 9.23, pp.84–85, lines 3577–3709

api.name: numberFieldBorelRegulator_apply
api.statement: At every σ the coordinate is precisely the Boₙ evaluation of σ_*(x).

api.name: numberFieldBorelRegulator_add
api.statement: The integral map is additive and annihilates every torsion element.

api.name: numberFieldBorelRegulator_localization
api.statement: For x in the integral K-group, r_Bo,ℚ(j_*(x)⊗1)=r_Bo(x); this property uniquely determines the rational field map.

tests.name: zero_and_torsion
tests.statement: r(0)=0 and m x=0 with m>0 implies m r(x)=0, hence r(x)=0 in a real vector space.

tests.name: localization_identity
tests.statement: On a nonzero rational K₅-class over ℚ, direct evaluation and integral rational localization both give t; an arbitrarily doubled inverse gives 2t.

tests.name: embedding_parity
tests.statement: An imaginary-quadratic class has divided coordinates (t,-t) in weight 2 and (t,t) in weight 3, exactly as in §1.1.

targets.name: numberFieldBorelRegulator_realIso
targets.statement: The real scalar extension K_(2n−1)(O_F)⊗ℝ→Vₙ(F) of the specified regulator is a real linear isomorphism, and r_Bo,ℚ is injective. For every finite extension E/F, r_E∘res=R∘r_F and r_F∘tr=T∘r_E, integrally where defined and after rational localization. Its kernel on the integral group is precisely torsion.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2

locator.where: Corollary 9.8, p.78, lines 3140–3150; Proposition 9.21 and Corollary 9.23, p.85; deligne_goncharov2005 §1.6, (1.6.3)–(1.6.10), pp.7–9, lines 320–428

api.name: numberFieldBorelRegulator_kernel
api.statement: An integral class maps to zero if and only if it has finite order.

api.name: numberFieldBorelRegulator_restriction
api.statement: The displayed restriction square uses R, with no averaging.

api.name: numberFieldBorelRegulator_transfer
api.statement: The displayed transfer square uses the full sum T over extensions of each embedding.

tests.name: q_dimensions
tests.statement: For ℚ, n=2 the source and target dimensions are 0; n=3 gives 1 and 1. The first equality alone proves no zeta value.

tests.name: quadratic_dimensions
tests.statement: For ℚ(i), n=2 and n=3 each give dimensions 1 and 1. For a real quadratic field n=3 gives 2 and 2.

tests.name: degree_two_composite
tests.statement: For ℚ(i)/ℚ at n=3, tr∘res acts by 2 and the target composite sends t to 2t; at n=2 the target sends (t,-t) to 0.

layers.title: Division algebras, rational gauges and arithmetic volume

targets.name: globalBrauerPeriodIndex
targets.statement: For every Brauer class α over a number field F, its period and index equal the least common multiple of the denominators of its finitely supported local invariants (including real invariants). In particular α of period a has a central division representative of dimension a². The zero class has period and index 1.
hypotheses: α is a Brauer class over F

locator.where: Theorem 1.5.36(iv) and proof of (iii), p.26, lines 1396–1446

api.name: globalBrauerPeriodIndex_local
api.statement: The denominator lcm computes the degree of the division representative.

api.name: globalBrauerPeriodIndex_split
api.statement: All local invariants vanish if and only if α=0.

api.name: globalBrauerPeriodIndex_degree
api.statement: For a≥1, a class of period dividing a has a central simple representative of degree a: if its division representative has degree d≥1, take M_(a/d)(D). The matrix size a/d is positive since d divides a.

tests.name: zero_class
tests.statement: The empty lcm is 1 and the representative is F of dimension 1. For a≥1 the same class is represented by M_a(F), of degree a and dimension a². At a=0 there is no nonzero matrix size and no central simple algebra of degree zero; that value is excluded.

tests.name: quaternion_pair
tests.statement: Invariants 1/2 at two finite places sum to 1=0 in ℚ/ℤ; period=index=2 and dimension is 4.

tests.name: cubic_pair
tests.statement: Invariants 1/3 and -1/3 have lcm 3, index 3 and dimension 9. Keeping only the first invariant gives sum 1/3 and no global class.

tests.name: dyadic_order_eight
tests.statement: The requested index 8 means dimension 64. A fixed unramified degree-eight dyadic prescription over ℚ is obstructed; permitting different local cyclic extensions is essential.

targets.name: existsDivisionAlgebraSplitAtInfinity
targets.statement: For every number field F and a≥2, construct a central division F-algebra D of dimension a² split at every infinite place. More precisely any finitely supported admissible family of local invariants of denominator lcm a and zero sum is realized by such a division algebra when all infinite invariants are zero.
hypotheses: For the refined statement the invariant family is admissible, finitely supported, zero at infinity, sums to zero and has denominator lcm a

api.name: existsDivisionAlgebraSplitAtInfinity_invariants
api.statement: The representative realizes each supplied local invariant.

api.name: existsDivisionAlgebraSplitAtInfinity_finrank
api.statement: Its dimension over F is exactly a².

api.name: existsDivisionAlgebraSplitAtInfinity_archimedean
api.statement: At every real or complex completion it is isomorphic to M_a of that completion.

tests.name: degree_two
tests.statement: Over ℚ, invariants 1/2 at 2 and 3 and 0 at infinity give degree 2, dimension 4, and a split real factor.

tests.name: degree_three
tests.statement: Invariants 1/3,-1/3 at two finite places give degree 3 and dimension 9, with every infinite invariant 0.

tests.name: archimedean_negative_control
tests.statement: The Hamilton algebra over ℚ has invariant 1/2 at infinity and dimension 4, but fails the infinite splitting hypothesis; the theorem does not identify it with the constructed indefinite quaternion algebra.

targets.name: borelArchimedeanGauge
targets.statement: Let H/F be a connected semisimple group of dimension h and let ω be a nonzero F-rational invariant top form. Define m∞=Δ_F^(−h/2)·∏_(v|∞)|ω|_v, with dx over ℝ and 2dxdy over ℂ and normalized squared complex absolute value. Let m_f=∏_(v finite)|ω|_v in the convergent semisimple gauge product. The product m∞·m_f is precisely the supplied Tamagawa measure. Transport to unscaled product measure multiplies an archimedean quotient volume by Δ_F^(h/2); replacing 2dxdy by dxdy additionally multiplies it by 2^(−hr₂).
hypotheses: H/F is connected semisimple of dimension h
ω is nonzero and invariant, defined over F

api.name: borelArchimedeanGauge_local
api.statement: m∞ is the displayed scalar multiple of the actual product of local gauge measures, not an arbitrary Haar measure.

api.name: borelArchimedeanGauge_scale
api.statement: For c∈Fˣ, replacing ω by cω scales m∞ by the product of its infinite absolute values.

api.name: borelArchimedeanGauge_tamagawa
api.statement: The infinite and finite factors multiply to the Tamagawa measure with zero geometric character lattice.

api.name: borelArchimedeanGauge_change
api.statement: A further linear chart change A multiplies coordinate density by |det A| with the local normalized absolute value; the stated discriminant and 2-power factors are retained.

tests.name: rational_form_scaling
tests.statement: Over ℚ, multiplying a top form by 2 multiplies m∞ by 2 and its 2-adic factor by 1/2; the global product multiplier is 1, regardless of h.

tests.name: imaginary_quadratic_density
tests.statement: For F=ℚ(i), Δ=4 and h=3, the discriminant factor is 1/8 and the complex coordinate factor is 2³=8. Their product against dxdy in three coordinates is 1.

tests.name: trivial_group
tests.statement: For h=0 and ω=1 the point has mass 1. With ω=2 over ℚ its infinite mass is 2 and its finite product is 1/2; the total mass remains 1.

tests.name: zero_form
tests.statement: ω=0 gives zero measure, so its quotient volume is 0 and cannot be in ℚ_>0·∏ζ; the nonzero hypothesis excludes it.

targets.name: normOneDivisionTamagawaOne
targets.statement: For every number field F, every a≥2, central division F-algebra D of dimension a² split at all infinite places, and nonzero F-rational invariant top form ω, identify the product m∞·m_f of §3.3 on H=SL₁(D) with the supplied Tamagawa measure. Its quotient by H(F), with counting measure, has mass 1 by gap:classical-tamagawa-proof. This specialization fixes the measure used in §3.6; the supplied numerical theorem also covers algebras ramified at infinity.
hypotheses: D is central division over F of dimension a²
D splits at every infinite place
ω is a nonzero F-rational invariant top form

locator.where: §3.3, Theorem 3.3.1, invoked in borel1977 p.619, line 227; waived locator

api.name: normOneDivisionTamagawaOne_positive
api.statement: The quotient mass is finite, strictly positive and equal to 1, not merely rational or finite.

tests.name: quaternion_input
tests.statement: For D=(-1,3) over ℚ the Hilbert symbols at 2, 3 and ∞ are -1, -1 and +1; all other local symbols are +1. Thus D is division, split over ℝ, h=3, and its normalized adelic mass is 1.

tests.name: cubic_input
tests.statement: For a degree-three division algebra split at infinity, h=8 and the normalized adelic mass is 1; matrix size does not multiply this mass by 3.

tests.name: rescale_two
tests.statement: For ω↦2ω over ℚ the product multiplier is 2·(1/2)=1, so the two predicted masses are both 1.

tests.name: torus_control
tests.statement: The norm-one torus of ℚ(i)/ℚ has dimension 1 and geometric character lattice ℤ, whereas the degree-two central division input has norm-one group dimension 3 and character lattice 0. The torus is excluded from this theorem.

targets.name: finiteGaugeEulerCorrection
targets.statement: For H=SL₁(D) as in §3.4, ω≠0 and a product compact open U=∏U_v, choose a finite S containing every nonsplit place, every nonintegral gauge place and every place with nonstandard level. At v∉S, |ω|_v(U_v)=∏_(j=2)^a(1−q_v^(−j)). At v∈S its mass is a positive rational. Define c_S(U,ω)=∏_(v∈S)(|ω|_v(U_v)/∏_(j=2)^a(1−q_v^(−j))). Then m_f(U)=c_S(U,ω)·∏_(j=2)^aζ_F(j)^(−1), with c_S positive rational and independent of enlarging S.
hypotheses: U is a product compact open, standard outside a finite set
q_v is the actual residue cardinality, hence q_v≥2

locator.where: Proposition 2.4 proof, p.619, lines 229–236

api.name: finiteGaugeEulerCorrection_positive
api.statement: Every denominator is a product of positive numbers 1−q_v^(−j); c_S is positive and rational.

api.name: finiteGaugeEulerCorrection_enlarge
api.statement: Adding a standard place multiplies c_S by 1.

api.name: finiteGaugeEulerCorrection_index
api.statement: If U′⊂U has finite index m then m_f(U′)=m_f(U)/m, including the finite exceptional factors.

tests.name: sl2_f2
tests.statement: At a standard q=2 place, #SL₂(𝔽₂)/2³=6/8=3/4=1−2^(−2). A unit local mass fails this normalization.

tests.name: bad_factor_retained
tests.statement: If an exceptional q=2 SL₂ level has gauge mass b, its correction is 4b/3. Deleting this place loses the factor 4b/3.

tests.name: no_q_one
tests.statement: At q=1 the putative factor 1−q^(−2) is 0 and its totalized inverse is 0; residue fields here have q≥2, so this value is excluded.

targets.name: arithmeticNormOneVolume
targets.statement: For H=SL₁(D) as in §3.4 and every arithmetic Γ⊂H(F), the quotient H∞/Γ is compact and vol_m∞(H∞/Γ)∈ℚ_>0·∏_(j=2)^aζ_F(j). If U is sufficiently small that Γ_U=H(F)∩(H∞×U) is torsion-free, the exact identity is τ(H)=vol_m∞(H∞/Γ_U)·m_f(U)=1. For any arithmetic Γ compare with Γ_U through their finite-index intersection. For the unscaled product archimedean gauge, the volume gains Δ_F^((a²−1)/2).
hypotheses: ω is a nonzero F-rational invariant top form
Γ is arithmetic; no torsion-free assumption for compactness or its volume class
For the exact product formula U is compact open and Γ_U is torsion-free

locator.where: §2.3 and Proposition 2.4, pp.618–619, lines 196–236

api.name: arithmeticNormOneVolume_level
api.statement: For sufficiently small U the displayed equality uses the actual subgroup Γ_U and measures derived from one ω.

api.name: arithmeticNormOneVolume_commensurable
api.statement: For Γ₀⊂Γ of index m, vol(H∞/Γ₀)=m·vol(H∞/Γ), with counting measure on discrete subgroups.

api.name: arithmeticNormOneVolume_gauge
api.statement: The discriminant and coordinate Jacobians are precisely those of §3.3.

tests.name: index_three
tests.statement: If U′ has index 3 in U, its finite mass is m_f(U)/3 and its infinite volume is 3 vol∞; both products equal 1.

tests.name: definite_quaternion_control
tests.statement: The Hamilton quaternion group has compact real points and is outside infinite splitting. A single principal-level fibre formula from strong approximation away from infinity cannot be assumed for it.

tests.name: split_control
tests.statement: For D=M₂(ℚ), SL₂(ℝ)/SL₂(ℤ) has finite volume but is noncompact; this algebra is not division. Division is essential for compactness.

tests.name: real_quadratic_gauge
tests.statement: For F=ℚ(√5), a=2 the unscaled product volume is 5^(3/2) times Borel’s volume; dropping that factor changes a rational multiple of ζ_F(2) to a different normalization.

targets.name: primitiveCohomologyDeterminantLine
targets.statement: For the connected nonnegative cohomology algebras over ℚ, ℝ or ℂ used here, form the degree-q indecomposable space using the supplied quotient Q(A)=A₊/(A₊)². For a finite-dimensional degree-q quotient construct its rational determinant line ∧^dim Q^q(A); in dimension zero its specified generator is 1. Apply this construction to compact dual, compact group, arithmetic group and invariant-form cohomology, retaining the maps on their actual quotient carriers.
hypotheses: A is one of the specified connected nonnegative cohomology algebras
The coefficient field is ℚ, ℝ or ℂ
The degree-q quotient is finite-dimensional for its determinant line

api.name: primitiveCohomologyDeterminantLine_dimension
api.statement: For quotient dimension d the top exterior power has dimension 1, and ∧⁰0 has its specified generator 1.

api.name: primitiveCohomologyDeterminantLine_map
api.statement: Every actual comparison induces its determinant map; the identity and composite induce the identity and composite determinant maps.

api.name: primitiveCohomologyDeterminantLine_baseChange
api.statement: The specified rational determinant line realifies and complexifies to the corresponding line of the scalar-extended quotient, preserving the empty generator.

tests.name: product_killed
tests.statement: In Λ(x₃,x₅), H⁸ has basis x₃x₅ and dimension 1 but Q⁸ has dimension 0; taking all cohomology would give 1 instead of 0.

tests.name: single_generator
tests.statement: For Λ(x₃), Q³=k·[x₃] has dimension 1 and Q⁶=0, since x₃²=0 in characteristic zero.

tests.name: trivial_algebra
tests.statement: For A=k concentrated in degree 0, Q=0 in every degree and its determinant is k with empty generator 1.

tests.name: even_generator
tests.statement: For k[u₂], Q²=k·[u₂] while Q⁴=0 although u₂²≠0. The quotient construction is not restricted to exterior algebras.

targets.name: invariantCompactDualComparison
targets.statement: Let G=Res_(F/ℚ)SL_a, K its standard connected maximal compact subgroup, X=G(ℝ)/K, Xᵘ its compact dual and Γ a torsion-free arithmetic subgroup. Construct the graded invariant-form comparison jℝ:H*(Xᵘ,ℝ)→H*(Γ,ℝ) and its maps on Q^q and determinant lines. Before real correction let μ be the complex comparison induced by identical extensions of forms to the complex tangent space; in degree q set jℝ=i^q μ. Construct also α:H*(Lie(G)_ℂ,ℂ)→H*(Gᵘ,ℂ) and β:H*(Lie(G)_ℂ,ℂ)→H*(G(ℝ)/Γ,ℂ).
hypotheses: K and the compact dual use the standard Cartan involution
prerequisites: roadmap:ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.F.5 and ALS.0.4–ALS.0.9 and ALS.5b.1

api.name: invariantCompactDualComparison_forms
api.statement: On each invariant form the comparison is the indicated identical complex extension followed by multiplication by i^q.

api.name: invariantCompactDualComparison_unit
api.statement: The degree-zero constant 1 maps to 1.

api.name: invariantCompactDualComparison_natural
api.statement: The comparison commutes with compatible block inclusions and arithmetic subgroup inclusions, hence induces the corresponding determinant maps.

api.name: invariantCompactDualComparison_real
api.statement: The corrected comparison has real values on real compact-dual classes; it is not obtained by forgetting an i-factor.

tests.name: unit
tests.statement: At q=0, i⁰=1 and jℝ(1)=1; the zero graded map fails this value.

tests.name: two_term_sign
tests.statement: For degree-one and degree-two factors the correction scalars are i and -1; their product is -i=i³, the degree-three correction.

tests.name: degree_five
tests.statement: At q=5 the correction is i⁵=i, whereas at q=3 it is -i. Using a constant -i in every odd degree fails weight 3.

tests.name: torsion_free_control
tests.statement: A C₂ stabilizer at a point has higher cohomology over 𝔽₂ in every nonnegative degree; plain point cohomology has only degree 0. Quotient-manifold descent here assumes torsion-free Γ and characteristic-zero coefficients.

targets.name: compactLiePrimitivePeriod
targets.statement: For n≥2 and a≥n, the degree-(2n−1) primitive cohomology of Lie(Res_(F/ℚ)SL_a) and of its compact group Gᵘ has dimension N. Relative to their rational determinant lines, the absolute determinant of α lies in ℚ_>0·π^(Nn)·Δ_F^(−(2n−1)/2). This statement concerns α on the specified rational Lie algebra and compact cohomology structures.
hypotheses: The rational lines are those of Borel §5.3, using the ordered embedding determinant

locator.where: Proposition 4.3, pp.623–625, lines 347–402; §5.3 and Proposition 5.4, pp.627–628, lines 462–480

api.name: compactLiePrimitivePeriod_basis
api.statement: Rational basis changes multiply the determinant by a nonzero rational absolute value.

api.name: compactLiePrimitivePeriod_stabilize
api.statement: The rational-line comparison commutes with restriction along a↦a+1 once the primitive degree survives.

tests.name: q_weight_two
tests.statement: For F=ℚ,n=2 the compact period class is π²·ℚ_>0; the degree-three suspended Chern generator pairs to -4π², with absolute ratio 4.

tests.name: q_weight_three
tests.statement: For F=ℚ,n=3 the compact determinant class is π³·ℚ_>0, rather than π²·ℚ_>0.

tests.name: imaginary_discriminant
tests.statement: For F=ℚ(i), Δ=4,n=2, the discriminant scalar is 4^(−3/2)=1/8 and the power is π⁴; it is nonzero, so cancelling the compact determinant is legitimate.

targets.name: divisionAlgebraPeriodCycle
targets.statement: For j≥1 choose D/F of degree j+1 split at infinity, and an odd a>(4N(j+1)²) large enough for its left regular representation D→M_a(F). For a torsion-free arithmetic Γ⊂Res SL_a, form Z_j=Res SL₁(D)(ℝ)/(Γ∩Res SL₁(D)(ℝ)) inside Y_a=G(ℝ)/Γ. It is a compact connected oriented manifold of dimension N(j²+2j). For the wedge η_j of all N rational primitive forms in degrees 3,5,…,2j+1, prove its restriction to Z_j is nonzero and |∫_(Z_j)β(η_j)|∈ℚ_>0·∏_(s=1)^jζ_F(s+1). Prove that wedging with η_(j−1) kills the ideal generated by the earlier primitive forms.
hypotheses: D has degree j+1 and splits at infinity
η_j uses rational generators of the primitive determinant lines in Borel §5.3

locator.where: Theorem 5.5 proof, pp.629–630, lines 499–551, especially equations (5)–(11)

api.name: divisionAlgebraPeriodCycle_dimension
api.statement: The group and compact cycle dimension is N((j+1)²−1)=N(j²+2j).

api.name: divisionAlgebraPeriodCycle_pullback
api.statement: At one embedding the top primitive wedge restriction factor is (j+1)^j; at all embeddings it is (j+1)^(jN), and is nonzero.

api.name: divisionAlgebraPeriodCycle_annihilate
api.statement: For every earlier generator x, η_(j−1)∧x=0. Thus changing primitive lifts by elements of the lower-generator ideal does not change the extracted period determinant.

tests.name: first_cycle
tests.statement: For F=ℚ,j=1, dim Z=3 and the restriction factor is 2¹=2; its nonzero absolute period is a rational multiple of ζ(2).

tests.name: second_cycle
tests.statement: For F=ℚ,j=2, dim Z=8, restriction factor 3²=9, and the period class is ζ(2)ζ(3)·ℚ_>0. Dividing by the first period isolates ζ(3).

tests.name: two_embeddings
tests.statement: For N=2,j=1 the dimension is 6 and the restriction factor is 2²=4, not 2.

tests.name: decomposable_control
tests.statement: In Λ(x₃,x₅), x₃∧x₃=0, so wedging with η₁=x₃ kills the ideal generated by x₃. A product with no repeated earlier generator cannot be dropped merely for having positive degree.

targets.name: fullGroupPrimitiveDeterminant
targets.statement: For n≥2 and a−1>4N(2n−1), let Γ⊂Res SL_a be torsion-free arithmetic and Y_a=G(ℝ)/Γ. In degree 2n−1 its indecomposable space has dimension N. The absolute determinant of β on the rational Lie determinant line into the rational determinant line of Q^(2n−1)H*(Y_a,ℚ) belongs to ℚ_>0·ζ_F(n). The assertion is compatible with stabilization and every commensurable arithmetic subgroup.

locator.where: Theorem 5.5, p.628, lines 481–494; determinant induction, pp.629–630, lines 499–551

api.name: fullGroupPrimitiveDeterminant_commensurable
api.statement: Restriction between finite-index arithmetic subgroups identifies the rational determinant lines in the stable range.

api.name: fullGroupPrimitiveDeterminant_stabilize
api.statement: Compatible matrix block inclusions identify the stated line comparison, including its nonzero determinant.

tests.name: first_quotient
tests.statement: The cumulative products at j=0 and j=1 are 1 and ζ_F(2), so their quotient is ζ_F(2), not 0.

tests.name: second_quotient
tests.statement: At j=2, ζ_F(2)ζ_F(3)/ζ_F(2)=ζ_F(3); ζ_F(2)>0 supplies the nonzero denominator.

tests.name: rank_zero_does_not_kill_full_line
tests.statement: For F=ℚ,n=2, the compact-dual primitive rank d is 0 but the full-group primitive rank N is 1. The ζ(2) period survives on this full line.

targets.name: compactFiberPrimitiveDeterminants
targets.statement: For F,n≥2, odd a with a−1>4N(2n−1), and torsion-free arithmetic Γ⊂Res SL_a, put q=2n−1 and Y=G(ℝ)/Γ. Construct the rational exact sequences 0→Q^qH*(Xᵘ,ℚ)→Prim H^q(Gᵘ,ℚ)→Prim H^q(K,ℚ)→0 and 0→Q^qH*(Γ,ℚ)→Q^qH*(Y,ℚ)→Prim H^q(K,ℚ)→0, with dimensions dₙ,N,N−dₙ. Their induced determinant-line decompositions are compatible, after complexification, with μ=β∘α⁻¹ and the identity on the compact-fibre factor. Their determinant identifications do not depend on choices of rational lifts.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2

locator.where: §5.2, pp.626–627, lines 440–461; Theorem 6.2 proof, p.632, equations (3)–(4), lines 581–585

api.name: compactFiberPrimitiveDeterminants_exact
api.statement: The kernel of restriction to the fibre is the base indecomposable image in the displayed stable degree.

api.name: compactFiberPrimitiveDeterminants_cancellation
api.statement: For each exact sequence det(full)=det(base)⊗det(fibre), and the comparison on det(fibre) is precisely the identity.

api.name: compactFiberPrimitiveDeterminants_lifts
api.statement: Adding a base lift changes a splitting by a block-unipotent matrix, with determinant 1.

tests.name: q_even_weight
tests.statement: For F=ℚ,n=2 the ranks are d=0,N=1,N−d=1. Cancelling the common rank-one fibre leaves the identity on ∧⁰0.

tests.name: q_odd_weight
tests.statement: For F=ℚ,n=3 the ranks are 1,1,0. The fibre determinant is the empty determinant 1.

tests.name: imaginary_ranks
tests.statement: For F=ℚ(i), in either parity the ranks are 1,2,1; the full determinant has two generators and the base has one.

tests.name: lift_change
tests.statement: The splitting change [[1,2],[0,1]] has determinant 1; replacing the fibre identity by multiplication by 2 would have determinant 2 and is excluded.

layers.title: Primitive determinant and the integral regulator lattice

targets.name: primitiveCompactDualDeterminant
targets.statement: For every F,n≥2,a−1>4N(2n−1) and torsion-free arithmetic Γ⊂Res SL_a, let Lᵘ=∧^dₙQ^(2n−1)H*(X_aᵘ,ℚ) and LΓ=∧^dₙQ^(2n−1)H*(Γ,ℚ). The actual real comparison induced by jℝ sends Lᵘ to c·LΓ for c∈ℚˣ·√Δ_F·π^(−Nn)·ζ_F(n). The determinant statement includes dₙ=0, with the actual empty comparison equal to 1. It is stable in a and compatible with passage to commensurable Γ.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2

locator.where: Theorem 6.2 and proof, pp.631–632, lines 567–589; Remark 6.3, lines 590–594

api.name: primitiveCompactDualDeterminant_empty
api.statement: If dₙ=0, both determinant lines are ℚ with empty generator 1 and the induced map sends 1 to 1.

api.name: primitiveCompactDualDeterminant_natural
api.statement: The actual induced determinant map commutes with stable restriction and finite-index arithmetic restriction.

api.name: primitiveCompactDualDeterminant_phase
api.statement: After the determinant correction the exponent E=r₂+(2n−1)dₙ−Nn equals (n−1)r₁ for odd n and -nr₁ for even n, hence is even.

tests.name: q_even
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=2, d=0 and the comparison determinant is 1, while √Δπ^(−2)ζ(2)=1/6. Their quotient is 6∈ℚˣ.

tests.name: q_odd_normalization
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=3, N=d=1, the raw determinant class is ζ(3)/π³ and E=2 gives i^E=-1. The renormalized regulator class has one additional π.

tests.name: imaginary_parities
tests.statement: For ℚ(i), N=2,r₁=0,r₂=1, E=0 for n=2 and n=3. The raw classes are 2ζ_F(2)/π⁴ and 2ζ_F(3)/π⁶, respectively.

tests.name: real_quadratic_even
tests.statement: For a real quadratic F,n=2, N=2,d=0,E=-4 and i^E=1. Its empty determinant 1 enforces √Δζ_F(2)/π⁴∈ℚˣ.

tests.name: rank_zero_rational_two
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=2, ζ(-1)=-1/12 and the §1.3 ratio is -1/2, giving ζ(2)/π²=1/6 and reciprocal 6. The comparison scalar is 1, and 6·(1/6)=1.

tests.name: rank_zero_rational_four
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=4, ζ(-3)=1/120 and the ratio is 3/4, giving ζ(4)/π⁴=1/90 and reciprocal 90; the empty determinant remains 1.

tests.name: rank_zero_all_real_even
tests.statement: For r₁=N,r₂=0 and n=2k≥2, d=0 and the exponent is -2kN; at N=2 it is -4k. Positivity of Δ_F, π and ζ_F(n) makes the rational class positive and its reciprocal defined.

tests.name: rank_zero_imaginary_negative_control
tests.statement: For ℚ(i), even n gives r₂=d=1, so the determinant has one row. Its covolume cannot be replaced by the empty value 1.

targets.name: borelHomotopyNormalization
targets.statement: Let R′_Bo be Burgos Definition 9.10’s covolume relative to the compact-dual homotopy lattice, and R_Bo the covolume after the character identification with Cₙ(F). Then R_Bo=(2π)^dₙ·ε(F,n)·R′_Bo, where ε(F,n)=2^r₁ when n≡3 mod4 and ε(F,n)=1 otherwise. The compact real-place homotopy generator maps with index 1 in degree 1 mod8 and index 2 in degree 5 mod8; a complex place contributes one conjugate pair. Construct the stable Cartan map C:SU/SO→SU by C(gSO)=g gᵗ and identify its free homotopy map with these indices, using the ordered generators.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2

locator.where: Lemma 9.18, Definition 9.19 and Remark 9.20, p.84, lines 3546–3614

api.name: borelHomotopyNormalization_realIndex
api.statement: At a surviving real place the integral index is 1 for n≡1 mod4 and 2 for n≡3 mod4.

api.name: borelHomotopyNormalization_complexPair
api.statement: Each complex place contributes one factor 2π, with no second independent embedding coordinate.

api.name: borelHomotopyNormalization_empty
api.statement: For dₙ=0 the factor is 1, since n is even and ε=1.

tests.name: q_two
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=2, d=0 and ε=1, giving R_Bo/R′_Bo=1.

tests.name: q_three
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=3, d=1 and ε=2: on π₅ the quotient SU→SU/SO is onto and C has index 2, so their composite is multiplication by 2. This gives R_Bo/R′_Bo=4π; a zero Cartan map would give 0.

tests.name: q_five
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=5, d=1 and ε=1: on π₉ the quotient has image 2ℤ and C has index 1, again giving composite multiplication by 2. Thus R_Bo/R′_Bo=2π. At the identity coset C(SO)=I. For g=diag(i,-i) and h=[[0,1],[-1,0]] in SO₂, both (gh)(gh)ᵗ and g gᵗ equal -I; the assignment [g]↦g would instead depend on the representative.

tests.name: imaginary_both
tests.statement: For an imaginary quadratic field, d=1,r₁=0 in either parity, so the ratio is 2π in both weights 2 and 3.

targets.name: borelRegulatorLattice
targets.statement: Let A=K_(2n−1)(O_F). Define Λₙ(F)=r_Bo(A) as a ℤ-submodule of Vₙ(F). The map A/A_tors→Λₙ is an isomorphism, Λₙ is discrete and spans Vₙ, and hence is an IsZLattice over ℝ. Define R_Bo(F,n)=ZLattice.covolume Λₙ for the coordinate Haar measure of §1.1. It is strictly positive and equals the absolute determinant of the regulator on any ordered ℤ-basis of A/A_tors. If dₙ=0 it is 1.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2

locator.where: Definition 9.19, p.84, lines 3577–3606; Corollary 9.8, p.78, lines 3140–3150

api.name: borelRegulatorLattice_mem
api.statement: v∈Λₙ if and only if there exists an integral K-class x with r_Bo(x)=v.

api.name: borelRegulatorLattice_quotientEquiv
api.statement: The integral regulator factors through A/A_tors and induces the specified isomorphism onto its image.

api.name: borelRegulatorLattice_isZLattice
api.statement: The submodule has discrete subtype topology and its real span is the whole Vₙ.

api.name: borelRegulatorLattice_covolume
api.statement: Its covolume is positive and is the absolute determinant in the §1.1 coordinates; unimodular changes of free basis preserve it.

tests.name: empty_lattice
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=2 the free group is 0, Λ={0} in {0}, and the empty determinant and covolume are both 1, not 0.

tests.name: rank_one_index
tests.statement: If x generates the free quotient and has coordinate t≠0, Λ=tℤ and R=|t|. Using 2x gives sublattice 2tℤ of index 2 and covolume 2|t|. For ℚ,n=3, §6.2 identifies ColemanIntegration’s Beilinson image as (t/2)ℤ, with covolume |t|/2; the common lattice theorem does not identify the two normalizations.

tests.name: finite_generation_not_enough
tests.statement: The finitely generated subgroup ℤ+√2ℤ⊂ℝ is not discrete although it spans. Its source has rank 2 and real extension cannot be an isomorphism to the rank-one target.

tests.name: rational_image
tests.statement: If d=1, the rational image is tℚ: t/m→0 with t/m≠0 for m≥1, so this image is not the integral lattice tℤ.

targets.name: borelRegulatorZetaCovolume
targets.statement: For every F and n≥2, R_Bo(F,n)∈ℚˣ·ζ_F*(1−n) and R_Bo(F,n)∈ℚ_>0·√Δ_F·π^(dₙ−Nn)·ζ_F(n). The rational regulator image is exactly the ℚ-span of Λₙ. For any ordered rational K-basis, its signed determinant in Tate-divided coordinates is in ℚˣ·√Δ_F·π^(dₙ−Nn)·ζ_F(n); its absolute determinant differs from R_Bo by a positive rational.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2

api.name: borelRegulatorZetaCovolume_leading
api.statement: There exists q∈ℚˣ with R_Bo=q·ζ_F*(1−n); the sign of q can be negative.

api.name: borelRegulatorZetaCovolume_positive
api.statement: The ratio to √Δ_F π^(dₙ−Nn) ζ_F(n) is a strictly positive rational.

api.name: borelRegulatorZetaCovolume_rationalImage
api.statement: The image of K_(2n−1)(F)⊗ℚ equals span_ℚ Λₙ as a subset of Vₙ.

api.name: borelRegulatorZetaCovolume_basis
api.statement: Replacing rational basis columns by A multiplies the signed determinant by det A, and the absolute determinant by |det A|.

tests.name: q_two_value
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=2, R=1 and ζ*(-1)=-1/12, so the leading-term rational factor is -12. The positive-integer factor is 6 since ζ(2)/π²=1/6.

tests.name: q_three_value
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=3 the exponent d−Nn is -2, so R is a nonzero rational multiple of ζ(3)/π²; using the unconverted cohomology determinant would give exponent -3.

tests.name: imaginary_values
tests.statement: For ℚ(i), √Δ=2 and d=1. The classes are 2ζ_F(2)/π³ at n=2 and 2ζ_F(3)/π⁵ at n=3.

tests.name: basis_sign
tests.statement: In dimension 2, swapping two rational basis columns has determinant -1, so signed determinant changes sign while R is unchanged. Multiplying one basis column by 2 doubles its absolute determinant.

targets.name: localizedBorelRegulatorLattices
targets.statement: For finite S, transport the regulator through ArithmeticKTheory’s actual equivalence K_(2n−1)(O_F)⊗ℚ≃K_(2n−1)(O_(F,S))⊗ℚ. The images of the two integral groups are equal full lattices in Vₙ, and their covolumes are equal. For any full ℤ-order R⊂F, transport through the actual rational inclusion into F; its integral image is a full lattice commensurable with Λₙ and its covolume has positive rational ratio to R_Bo. All extension, transfer and S-enlargement squares use the supplied maps and the §1.2 target maps.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2
S is a finite set of finite places
For the order assertion R is a full ℤ-order in F

locator.where: §6.4, pp.632–633, lines 595–615; arithmetic localization import from ArithmeticKTheory §§3.3–3.4

api.name: localizedBorelRegulatorLattices_enlarge
api.statement: S-enlargement and composition agree with the actual localized K-map; in higher odd degree they preserve the integral image and its covolume exactly.

api.name: localizedBorelRegulatorLattices_index
api.statement: A sublattice of index m has covolume m times the larger lattice’s covolume.

tests.name: empty_S
tests.statement: At S=∅ the transported map is r_Bo and the covolume ratio is 1.

tests.name: dyadic_allowed
tests.statement: For S containing a prime above 2 and n=2 or 3 the rational rank remains dₙ. No factor is deleted merely because its residue characteristic is 2.

tests.name: degree_one_control
tests.statement: For ℤ→ℤ[1/2] in degree 1, the unit ranks are 0 and 1, so the transported finite-rank equivalence asserted for 2n−1≥3 cannot be extended to K₁.

tests.name: index_law
tests.statement: For two lattices with common sublattice indices 2 and 3, their covolume ratio is 3/2 in the corresponding order; rational commensurability does not imply equality.

layers.title: Point Deligne realization and the Beilinson comparison

targets.name: pointDeligneEmbeddingModel
targets.statement: For n>0 define the real vector-space model Dₙ(F)=(∏_(σ∈Σ_F)ℂ/ℝ(n))^conj. Define P_(n−1)(z)=(z+(-1)^(n−1)conj z)/2. It annihilates ℝ(n), induces ℂ/ℝ(n)≃ℝ(n−1), and gives Dₙ(F)≃Vₙ(F). Identify this concrete model with H¹_D(Spec(F)×_ℚℝ,ℝ(n)) through the supplier’s Deligne point computation and finite-disjoint-union and real-descent maps.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n>0
The Deligne identification uses the independent universal Deligne carrier

locator.where: Examples 10.4–10.5 and Remark 10.6, p.91, lines 3955–4008

api.name: pointDeligneEmbeddingModel_projection
api.statement: The map from a coset [z] is P_(n−1)(z), independent of the representative.

api.name: pointDeligneEmbeddingModel_inverse
api.statement: The inverse sends a vector of ℝ(n−1) to its coset in ℂ/ℝ(n); both composites are identities.

api.name: pointDeligneEmbeddingModel_lattice
api.statement: The natural point integral structure is carried to Cₙ, with selected generator (2πi)^(n−1) having coordinate 1.

api.name: pointDeligneEmbeddingModel_natural
api.statement: Restriction and trace on points become exactly R and T of §1.2.

tests.name: weight_two_projection
tests.statement: For n=2, P₁(1)=0 and P₁(i)=i; the nonzero class of i survives modulo ℝ(2)=ℝ.

tests.name: weight_three_projection
tests.statement: For n=3, P₂(1)=1 and P₂(i)=0; projection onto the imaginary axis would reverse these values.

tests.name: coset_inverse
tests.statement: For n=2, z=1+i has P₁(z)=i and z-P₁(z)=1∈ℝ(2); for n=3 it has P₂(z)=1 and difference i∈ℝ(3). Both quotient inverse identities hold.

tests.name: real_point_fixed_space
tests.statement: At F=ℚ,n=2 the conjugation-fixed quotient is 0; at n=3 it is one-dimensional. Taking invariants on embeddings alone would give a false weight-two real direction.

targets.name: borelBeilinsonComparison
targets.statement: Let r_Be be the independently constructed universal Beilinson regulator on K_(2n−1)(F), with suspended Chern-character normalization and target identified by §6.1. On O_F and on rationalized field K-theory, r_Bo=2r_Be. For the same ordered rational K-basis and embedding coordinates det(r_Bo)=2^dₙdet(r_Be), including the empty determinant. The maps commute with restriction and the full embedding trace for transfers.
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2
r_Be is the supplied universal Chern/Deligne map, not a map defined by the claimed equation

locator.where: Definitions 10.7–10.8, p.94, lines 4087–4106; Theorem 10.9 and proof, pp.95–97, lines 4133–4245

api.name: borelBeilinsonComparison_map
api.statement: Equality holds on the actual universal regulator after the explicit point target identification.

api.name: borelBeilinsonComparison_det
api.statement: The determinant ratio is exactly 2^dₙ for the same basis and coordinate order.

api.name: borelBeilinsonComparison_lattice
api.statement: The images of the same integral free quotient have covolumes related by R_Bo=2^dₙ R_Be; arbitrary unrelated lattices are not compared.

tests.name: rank_zero_comparison
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=2 both determinant maps send 1 to 1 and 2⁰=1; the comparison supplies no ζ(2) value by itself.

tests.name: rank_one_comparison
tests.statement: For ℚ,n=3 or any imaginary quadratic F in weight 2 or 3, d=1 and the ordered determinant ratio is 2.

tests.name: rank_two_comparison
tests.statement: For a real quadratic F,n=3, d=2 and the ratio is 4, not 2.

tests.name: zero_map_control
tests.statement: In a rank-one example the real regulator is an isomorphism with determinant t≠0, so r_Be=0 would give 2·0=0≠t. The independent Chern normalization also excludes a rescaling of r_Be.

targets.name: borelAdamsWeight
targets.statement: For every F,n≥2 and integer a≥1, the supplied Adams operation ψ^a acts on K_(2n−1)(F)⊗ℚ as a^n·id. The same holds on rationalized O_F K-theory through localization, and the determinant of ψ^a on that space is a^(ndₙ).
hypotheses: n is an integer with n ≥ 2
a is an integer with a≥1
ψ^a is the supplied scheme/ring Adams operation

locator.where: Published §1.6, p.9, lines 429–440, after equation (1.6.10)

api.name: borelAdamsWeight_regulator
api.statement: The actual regulator intertwines ψ^a with multiplication by a^n.

api.name: borelAdamsWeight_det
api.statement: The determinant is a^(ndₙ), with value 1 on the zero space.

tests.name: q_weight_three
tests.statement: At F=ℚ,n=3,a=2, ψ² acts by 8 and its determinant is 8 on the rank-one rational K₅.

tests.name: real_quadratic_weight_three
tests.statement: At a real quadratic F,n=3,a=2, ψ² acts by 8 on two coordinates, so its determinant is 8²=64.

tests.name: zero_rank
tests.statement: At F=ℚ,n=2,a=2 the space is 0 and its determinant is 2^(2·0)=1, not 4.

tests.name: identity_operation
tests.statement: At a=1 the scalar and determinant are both 1 for every dₙ. The theorem makes no claim for a=0.

suppliers.what: Actual Quillen groups, the specified plus/Q comparison and finite-projective transfer with naturality.
Homotopy-fibre long exact sequence, stable GL plus H-space, and rational primitive Hurewicz for path-connected finite-type rational H-spaces.
Finite generation for number rings and finite S; actual rational localization; stable arithmetic invariant-form comparison, primitive generators and Borel ranks, independent of regulator values.
Relative CE cochains, actual symmetric spaces and arithmetic quotients, manifold and finite-stabilizer comparisons, de Rham identification.
Differentiable and continuous cochains on the native carriers and the finite-dimensional coefficient van Est comparison with full compact subgroup.
Scalar restriction, quotient integration, gauges and Tamagawa normalization, SL₁(D), anisotropic compactness and simply connected strong approximation.
Normalized local Brauer invariants, restriction multiplied by local degree, finite support and exact number-field Brauer invariant sequence.
Grunwald–Wang with its dyadic exceptional class, used only through the additional full-local-degree contract.
The continued Dedekind function, its germ regularity, completed functional equation and agreement with the pinned convergent function.

Actual compact-Lie primitive/transgression comparisons, multiplicative cohomological Serre spectral sequences and rational universal Chern characters; integral homotopy calibration and invariant-form filtration comparison are separate gaps.
Complex Bott and real coefficient maps, including complexification and realification, with fixed generators.
Oriented integration, Stokes and multiplicative de Rham/period comparison.
Actual higher Adams operations and their affine Quillen comparison for regular Noetherian finite-dimensional schemes with ample family.

Native bundle Serre filtration, monodromy and Leray–Hirsch applications, with CharacteristicClasses C5a.5 supplying the multiplicative cohomological sequence and gap:multiplicative-serre-comparison its invariant-form comparison.
Siegel–Klingen rationality at the trivial character for comparison with the totally real rank-zero example; not an input to the general primitive-period proof.

consumers.what: §§2.3,3.7–3.8,4.4 consume §§2.1–2.3,5.2–5.4 and 6.2; §4.7 uses §5.1’s rank-zero clause together with IntegralIwasawaTheory §6.0. Its explicit factorial and Hurewicz calibration and π^(n−1) conversion stay there.
PS.3.2a imports §§2.1–2.3 and 6.1–6.3 for its fundamental-line and mixed Tate applications.
§3.6 imports the number-field period–index theorem §3.1 in its PGL descent comparison.
§1.5 uses the embedding rational-image theorem indirectly through Polylogarithms; no Habiro-symbol or torsion assertion is a premise here.
§L3.Fc.1 uses §§2.2–2.3 and 5.3 for the complex regulator lattice theorem, and §6.2 for its Beilinson normalization; its pairings and discriminant/regulator determinants remain there.

gaps.title: Finite-stage arithmetic comparison with an explicit range
gaps.detail: The finite-stage form extends ArithmeticKTheory §3.4’s stable arithmetic and relative-Lie comparison and its primitive generators. Supply actual invariant-form comparison maps, stabilization and rational finite-index restriction; for Res SL_a over F the range a−1>4Nq must imply isomorphism through degree q. Finite-type is used only on the arithmetic plus H-space, not on GL(ℂ) with its discrete topology.
gaps.needs: Supply, for every number field F of degree N, a≥2, G=Res_(F/ℚ)SL_a with its standard maximal compact K and every arithmetic Γ⊂G(ℚ), the actual invariant-form maps H^q(Lie G,K;ℝ)→H^q(Γ;ℝ) for q∈ℕ, compatible with block stabilization and finite-index restriction, and bijective whenever a−1>4Nq.
gaps.section: §3.4, explicit finite-stage form of the stable comparison

gaps.title: Integral Bott-to-suspended-Chern calibration
gaps.detail: Use the ordered complex suspension of C6 item 3 and the actual clutching map on TopologicalKTheory T4’s Bott coefficient u=O(-1)−1, with ch(u)=−v. For n≥2 set εₙ=(-1)^n clutch(u^n) in stable π_(2n−1)SU. The rational evaluation uses the integral Hurewicz image; multiplication by (2πi)^n gives the evaluation with Tate coefficient ℝ(n) (burgos2002, Proposition 9.22, p.85, lines 3670–3688). The real-place homotopy indices are the separate target §5.2 here, using TopologicalKTheory T7 item 1.
gaps.needs: Supply s(chₙ)(Hur εₙ)=1 for n≥2, for the rational character chₙ of CharacteristicClasses C6 item 2 and εₙ=(-1)^n clutch(u^n), u=O(-1)−1, with the ordered suspension of CharacteristicClasses C6 item 3 and the (x,y)↦x+iy orientation of TopologicalKTheory T4; equivalently s(chₙᵗʷ)(Hur εₙ)=(2πi)^n for chₙᵗʷ=(2πi)^n·chₙ.

gaps.title: The variable-local-extension consequence of Grunwald–Wang
gaps.detail: ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4.5b–R02.4.6 retains the exact exceptional class for fixed character prescriptions. Supply the consequence used in Poonen’s proof: for any a≥1 and finite set of finite places, a cyclic degree-a extension may be chosen with local degree a at those places, with the local extensions allowed to vary, and with selected real places complex when a is even. No assertion of arbitrary prescribed unramified dyadic extensions is made.
gaps.needs: Supply, for every number field F, a≥1, finite set S of finite places and set R of real places (R empty when a is odd), a cyclic extension L/F of degree a with [L_w:F_v]=a for every v∈S and w|v, and every place of R complex in L; the local extensions may vary.

gaps.title: The structure of the supplied norm-one group
gaps.detail: AdelicAlgebraicGroups §3.4 explicitly constructs SL₁(D), its semisimplicity and quotient compactness. Strong approximation in §4.2 additionally needs absolute almost simplicity and simple connectedness. Supply these properties by base change to SL_a for every central division algebra of degree a≥2; no new group carrier is needed.
gaps.needs: Supply absolute almost simplicity and simple connectedness of the existing SL₁(D) carrier.

gaps.title: Rational masses of compact opens at ramified places
gaps.detail: Extend AdelicAlgebraicGroups §2.4’s smooth integral-model masses (with the gauge a generator of invariant top forms) and gauge scaling to rationality of every compact-open mass for every rational invariant form at an arbitrary finite place. Require the extension for smooth affine algebraic groups over nonarchimedean characteristic-zero local fields with finite residue field, using the fixed coordinate Haar normalization. Include finite-index comparison and compatibility with a single global rational gauge; a hyperspecial-only theorem cannot discharge the ramified factors.
gaps.needs: Supply positive rational local gauge masses for all compact opens, including ramified finite places.
gaps.section: Part II, rational gauge masses extending §2.4

gaps.title: Integral finite generation for nonmaximal orders
gaps.detail: ArithmeticKTheory §3.4 explicitly supplies the rational inclusion equivalence for every order. The integral image being a lattice also needs finite generation, not only a rational dimension. Supply finite generation of K_m(R) for every full ℤ-order R in a number field and m≥2, or an equally strong finite-index image theorem. Number-ring and finite-S finite generation in §3.3 cannot silently be applied to a singular nonmaximal order.
gaps.needs: Supply finite generation or a finite-index integral comparison for higher K-groups of all number-field orders.
gaps.section: extension of ArithmeticKTheory §§3.2–3.4 to all full ℤ-orders

gaps.title: Independent universal Deligne and Chern realization
gaps.detail: For varieties, provide actual real Deligne cohomology and rational Chern regulators, including the point, finite disjoint unions, real descent, universal bundle class and maps from actual Quillen K-theory, naturality for embeddings and finite transfers, and chₙψ^a=a^n chₙ. This construction is independent of the Borel zeta-value and explicit polylogarithm comparisons. Its point case supplies ColemanIntegration §L3.Fc.1’s reg_∞ through §§6.1–6.2 here.
gaps.needs: Supply the independent universal Chern/Deligne regulator and its point, transfer and Adams compatibility.

gaps.title: The infinitesimal comparison used in Burgos’s local proof
gaps.detail: Over the actual universal classifying model, compare normalized cosimplicial functions/forms on the first infinitesimal classifying nerve with CE and Weil complexes, including evaluation into continuous cohomology and the Deligne cone projection. Fix the coefficient normalizations independently of the factor-two conclusion (burgos2002, Chapter 8, Propositions 8.9, 8.10, 8.14; Theorem 10.9 proof, lines 4172–4190).
gaps.needs: Supply normalized infinitesimal classifying-space CE/Weil comparisons with the Deligne cone projection.

gaps.title: The generic graded augmentation quotient
gaps.detail: CharacteristicClasses C5a.2 already constructs the invariant-polynomial augmentation quotient and its coefficient and generator changes. Its generalization to every connected nonnegative graded commutative algebra, needed for cohomology of arithmetic quotients and compact duals, belongs to its Part II. Supply Q(A)=A₊/(A₊)², the homogeneous quotient, quotient universal property, map and base-change laws, and the exterior-generator comparison. Section 4.1 constructs only the cohomological determinant adapters, not a second generic augmentation quotient.
gaps.needs: Supply one generic graded indecomposable functor extending the existing invariant-polynomial construction.
gaps.section: Part II, general graded quotient API extending C5a.2

gaps.title: Invariant-form comparison of the cohomological Serre filtrations
gaps.detail: Use CharacteristicClasses C5a.5’s multiplicative cohomological Serre spectral sequence. For a number field F, a≥2, G=Res_(F/ℚ)SL_a, its standard connected maximal compact K and torsion-free arithmetic Γ, compare the bundles K→Gᵘ→Xᵘ and K→G(ℝ)/Γ→K\G(ℝ)/Γ with the compact-Lie-subalgebra filtration on absolute Lie cochains. The maps α and β of §4.2 must preserve that filtration and induce the same restriction to K (borel1977, §3.5, p.622, lines 328–337).
gaps.needs: Supply, for a number field F of degree N, n≥2, odd a with a−1>4N(2n−1) and torsion-free arithmetic Γ⊂Res_(F/ℚ)SL_a, the comparison of the C5a.5 spectral sequences of K→Gᵘ→Xᵘ and K→G(ℝ)/Γ→K\G(ℝ)/Γ with the Lie-cochain filtration, preserving edge restriction and the identity on the common compact fibre, where G=Res_(F/ℚ)SL_a and K is its standard connected maximal compact.

gaps.title: Index divisibility for every finite splitting extension
gaps.needs: For any field K, finite-dimensional central simple K-algebra A and finite field extension L/K splitting A, provide index(A)∣[L:K] on Tau Ceti’s native index and splitting-field carriers, without a separability restriction.
gaps.detail: SemisimpleAlgebras Layer 6 and TauCeti.Algebra.CentralSimple.Index provide an index-degree splitting field but do not state divisibility of every finite splitting degree by the index. Extend that generic theory in Part II. For a division factor D of degree d and a splitting L, restrict the M_d(L)-module L^d to D; finite-dimensionality over the division ring gives d²k=d[L:K], hence d divides [L:K]. The number-field proof in §3.1 consumes this input and the existing index-degree splitting field, rather than constructing a second index theory.
gaps.section: Part II, finite splitting-degree divisibility extending Layer 6
